# Workflow instructions

Read [the development reference](../../docs/development.md) before editing reusable workflows, pins or release behavior.

- Reusable workflows expose typed `workflow_call` inputs and minimal permissions. Local `./` action references resolve against the caller. Fetch repository-owned helpers, hash manifests and default npm lockfiles from `job.workflow_repository` at `job.workflow_sha`. Preserve `lint-text`'s `use-consumer-versions: true` opt-in to the caller's reviewed lockfile.
- Install required tools explicitly unless their runner-provided use is documented in the development reference. Keep shellcheck available to actionlint and preserve the self-test that demonstrates shell blocks are actually checked.
- Workflow steps driving `install-pinned-tool.sh` set only the installer variables the tool uses. Do not add the `CHECKSUM: ""` blanks the composite actions carry: a called workflow does not inherit the caller's `env`, so there is nothing to shadow, and the installer rejects a second checksum source anyway. `lint-text.yml` and `run-scrut-tests.yml` both rely on this.
- Argument, flag, path-list and target-list inputs use `env:` plus `read -r -a` into a quoted array: simple space-delimited values, without quoting, escaping, glob or variable expansion, and a multi-line value is rejected rather than truncated to its first line. Preserve this interface instead of adopting composite actions' newline-delimited convention; #96 settled that, and the development reference records why. Only the documented command inputs (`scrut-setup-cmd`, `scrut-build-cmd`, `build-command`) may interpolate into `run:`; the `workflow-arg-binding` job enforces that list.
- Every `actions/checkout` sets `persist-credentials: false`, so the job's token does not outlive the checkout in `.git/config`. The single exception is the Homebrew tap checkout in `release-rust-binaries.yml`, which sets `true` for the push step that follows it and is named so the exemption keys on something stable. `gh` and `peter-evans/create-pull-request` authenticate from a token they are handed, so neither needs it. `tests/check-checkout-credentials.mjs`, run by the `checkout-credentials` job, enforces this.
- `publish-to-npm.yml`, `publish-to-npm-with-oidc.yml` and `deploy-to-pages.yml` carry byte-identical install steps, and the two publish workflows byte-identical lockfile probes, because a called workflow cannot reach a composite action by a `./` path. `check-npm-publish.mjs` fails if a copy drifts. Keep the two publish workflows separate: a caller must grant everything the workflow it calls declares, including for a job its own `if:` will skip, so merging them would put `id-token: write` on every token-path caller. Publish jobs keep `package-manager-cache: false`; the Pages build keeps its cache. The OIDC workflow's `environment` input is load-bearing, not decoration: the claim npm matches comes from that job, and a calling job may not declare an environment.
- Consumer Rust toolchains come from explicit `rust-version`, the configured `rust-toolchain-file`, or the legacy `rust-toolchain` fallback; fail if none yields a value. clap-validator's test pins are fixtures, not defaults to add to the tool-version audit.
- `run-go-ci.yml` consumers must provide enabled `vet`, `test`, `lint`, `build` and `fmt` Make targets. `fmt` checks and fails on unformatted code; it does not write.
- Keep installer self-tests across Linux amd64, Linux arm64 and macOS arm64. cspell has two dictionary fixtures and both are load-bearing: the action-level one is written outside the checkout so resolution cannot come from an ordinary `node_modules` walk, and `tests/fixtures/cspell-extra-dict/` is committed so `lint-text.yml`'s `cspell-config` can prove a skipped install fails. Keep the committed fixture out of this repo's own `cspell.json` scan and out of every manifest. The scrut fixture proves uv reaches `PATH`; clap-validator checks installation, cache hits and rejected pins.
- Update `../../docs/workflows/<name>.md` and the root component index together with workflow interfaces. Release notes come from the matching CHANGELOG section; tag CI creates the release.
